model.rationale: Every available signal points the same way: a district leaning ten points Democratic, a well-funded incumbent, a challenger with almost no resources, and markets pricing the race near 97% Democratic. With no contrary evidence, the forecast stays at Safe D with a margin in the low twenties.
model.watch: A late wave of outside spending against Morelle or an unusually strong Republican national environment could narrow the margin, though an upset would require a large shift.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.

overview:
Joseph Morelle, the Democratic incumbent, enters the general election as a heavy favorite in a Rochester-area district that leans about ten points Democratic. He has raised roughly $2.2 million and holds more than $500,000 in cash, while Republican Virginia McIntyre has raised about $47,000 with under $2,000 on hand. No outside groups are spending against Morelle, and prediction markets put Democratic winning chances near 97%.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, incumbency, and the money gap. Those factors all point in the same direction, suggesting a comfortable Democratic margin in the low twenties. The main uncertainty is typical for lightly polled races: turnout patterns or a late challenger surge could narrow the result, but an upset would require a substantial shift in conditions.
